record.original_question: Are cryptosystems built from infinite polycyclic groups resistant to quantum cryptanalysis? Equivalently, can one show that polycyclic group-based cryptosystems remain secure against quantum algorithms, especially given that no quantum algorithms are currently known for infinite groups?

evidence.quote: Of particular interest is to show that cryptosystems using infinite polycyclic groups are resistant to cryptanalysis on a quantum computer.
(10) Are polycyclic group-based cryptosystems resistant to quantum algorithms?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polycyclic group is a group $G$ admitting a subnormal series $G = G_0 \triangleright G_1 \triangleright \cdots \triangleright G_n = \{1\}$ in which every quotient $G_i/G_{i+1}$ is cyclic. Such a group is called infinite if $|G| = \infty$. Polycyclic groups are finitely presented and have solvable word, conjugacy, and isomorphism problems, which makes them candidates for platform groups in non-commutative public-key cryptography (e.g., Diffie–Hellman-type key exchange and ElGamal-type encryption based on the conjugacy search problem, the twisted conjugacy problem, or the word problem in $G$).

A cryptosystem is said to be resistant to quantum cryptanalysis if no polynomial-time quantum algorithm (in the size of the public parameters) can recover the secret key or break the underlying hard problem with non-negligible advantage.

Problem: Determine whether public-key cryptosystems whose security reduces to algorithmic problems (such as the conjugacy search problem, the twisted conjugacy problem, or the subgroup membership problem) in infinite polycyclic groups are resistant to quantum cryptanalysis. Equivalently, either exhibit a polynomial-time quantum algorithm that solves these underlying search problems in a generic family of infinite polycyclic groups, or prove that no such quantum algorithm exists (for instance, by establishing a quantum hardness lower bound or by reducing a presumed quantum-hard problem to one of these problems).
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2022–2024 surveys on group-based cryptography in the quantum era (e.g., Kahrobaei–Flores, eprint 2022/1161), no polynomial-time quantum algorithm is known for the relevant search problems in infinite polycyclic groups, and the question of provable quantum resistance for polycyclic group-based cryptosystems remains an open research direction. Recent work has analyzed the complexity of conjugacy search in specific polycyclic and matrix groups, but no general quantum-resistance proof or quantum break has been established.

status_evidence.title: Group-based Cryptography in the Quantum Era
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing polycyclic group-based cryptosystems and the lack of known quantum algorithms attacking them, motivating their study as post-quantum candidates.
status_evidence.claim: No quantum polynomial-time algorithm is currently known to break polycyclic group-based cryptosystems, and the question of their quantum resistance remains an active open problem.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of Conjugacy Search in some Polycyclic and Matrix Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Analyses the classical complexity of the conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups; does not establish quantum resistance.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies classical complexity of the underlying problems but does not resolve quantum resistance.
